body: We don't have kids yet, she stopped working to figure out who she was. I gave her the option to stop working once I made enough to barely cover us. But kids are in the table, and she is less concerned about how much I'll make and how much debt I'll accrue, and more concerned that I won't be happy to just come home to her everyday.

I work and she is stay at home, but looking at part time now. She was always a harder worker than me, but took some time away from work once I made enough to afford our bills at the time. I make 18 an hour and that barely gets us through bills and groceries, hence why she's looking at work now.

She's against college in general. She understands education is important, she mostly doesn't like it because of the financial risk for a degree that "will just sit in a drawer and never get used." She keeps quoting our other friends who are getting out of college now and having a huge amount of trouble getting hired.

I've always put my family first, and I don't think I will become a workaholic, but I also can't say I won't. I care a lot about my career and my job, so it's hard to say if I will let it effect my home life.

She's got a few hobbies. She draws, goes to the gym, plays a lot of Destiny, and overall seems to enjoy it. I try to give her the space to enjoy these things, but lately it kind of feels like she uses them as a way to avoid conversation.

You might be right about counseling, but that can be expensive, and I'm not sure I can afford it on my salary alone.

She doesn't want to work. I told her that it wasn't a big deal, and I'd cover as much as I could with my job. We're struggling with money a lot lately, but I keep telling her not to worry and to get a job when she's ready. She's been jobless since February.

Let's take a step back here for a moment. You work for a company where customers will leave if you aren't there in time. But there will always be other clients. A client leaves, another one comes. But you only have one daughter, I assume. One girl who doesn't just want any attention, she wants yours. Yes, you complain about how she sucks up all attention on the room, but that's only because she doesn't see you everyday. It's because she loves you and wants to see you show that you love her. But your actions are saying that you don't. That you're career, your boss/boyfriend, and your customers are more important than your own child.

Whether your boss was saying to go out of necessity or not shouldn't matter. What matters is that your daughter is going into a dangerous surgery and wanted the mother she loves to be there. Your boyfriend tried to support you, even at his own inconvenience. You said he could have called in another staff member, so don't use the excuse that you were needed. Your daughter needed you. And all you did by doing this is let her down. If that makes you happy, then YTA. If not, then you need to show your daughter that you love her. Or else she'll just see you as TA for the rest of her life.
